transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Former President Barack Obama campaigned in Ohio
and Michigan yesterday, rallying Democrats ahead
of next week's midterm elections.
In Detroit, Obama threw his support
behind U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
Michigan Public Radio's Colin Jackson reports.
Obama's speech came as Michigan Democrats try to lock down
their base on the first day
of statewide early in-person voting.
Republicans have tried to paint El-Sayed, who was born and raised
in Michigan, as caring more about Arab countries
than Michigan communities.
Obama says that playbook sounds familiar.
>> They may even use your name or your faith to sound --
I suggest that you are dangerous and less than trustworthy
and less patriotic and less American than they are.
We have seen this movie before, as starred in it.
>> Democrats and Republicans see Michigan as must-win
on the path to a U.S. Senate majority.
President Donald Trump is also campaigning
on Michigan this weekend.
For NPR News, I'm Colin Jackson.
>> The Justice Department is planning to send 1,000 election
monitors to polling places across the country
for the midterms.
Oregon Secretary of State Tobias Reid
says federal observers must follow state rules.
>> They have to sign our observer agreement
and agree to abide by the rules laid out in that document
while they are in our building.
>> In Oregon, election officials say federal observers
will be treated like anyone else watching the process.
The Justice Department says its goal
is to protect election integrity.
It also denies plans to send armed agents to polling sites.
Flood watches remain in effect today in parts of the Southwest.
NPR's Ava Berger reports severe flooding
across parts of Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico,
and Utah have displaced hundreds of people.
>> It took only 22 days for Juana Puga's house
in Utah to flood again.
>> They were saying, like, "Why again?"
>> Puga, her husband, and five young kids
just moved back to their house in Hurricane Utah
on October 1st after a flood in August.
On Thursday morning,
Puga stood in ankle-deep brownish water again.
She describes it as a nightmare.
Her home is one of more than 100 damaged in the city.
>> After cleaning up a little bit,
I mean, we're still very sad about our homes,
but it's just we just lift each other up and like,
"Okay, we already did this. We can do it again."
>> Ava Berger, NPR News.
>> The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to an $800 million
settlement with more than 1,000 people
who say clergy sexually abused them.
It's the second largest settlement
involving a Catholic Archdiocese in the U.S.
This is NPR News.
For more than a month, a large gray shark
has captured the attention of people in South Korea.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports authorities
have tried repeatedly but unsuccessfully
to coax the shark out of a canal in a city park.
>> The 11-and-a-half-foot-long shark is named Bukangi
after the North Port Park in the city of Busan,
where he's attracted over 1.7 million visitors
since September 19th.
Busan city government even appointed Bukangi
as its honorary ambassador.
After a third attempt to herd Bukangi out to sea,
the shark disappeared on Friday morning.
South Korean media report he was sighted again on Saturday
near a port passenger terminal about a mile from the canal.
Authorities say Bukangi appears to be in good health
and they hope he's transitioning out of the canal
towards the sea.
Some observers, though, are worried
that Bukangi had to dive out of sight
to dodge an oil slick on the water's surface.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News sold.
>> Voters in Brazil are heading to the polls today
in a closely contested presidential runoff.
leftist President Lula da Silva
is facing right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro,
the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.
The latest polls show the candidates running about even.
Bolsonaro finished ahead in the first round,
but Lula has narrowed the gap.
High living costs and crime
have been central issues in the campaign.
Bolsonaro has promised tougher crime policies
and pledged to free his father,
who was convicted of plotting a coup
after losing the last presidential election.
This is NPR News.
>> This message comes from EasyCater,
making it easy for organizations to order food

topics.text: Obama campaigns in Detroit for Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed ahead of Michigan midterms
Justice Department plans 1,000 election monitors at polls; Oregon sets observer rules
Flooding in Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico, and Utah displaces hundreds; Hurricane, Utah homes damaged again
Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement with over 1,000 clergy abuse survivors
Giant shark Bukangi evades repeated rescue attempts in Busan canal, reportedly sighted near port
Brazil votes in closely contested presidential runoff between Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro
